description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Match' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. PvP / match system configuration, grouped by battle mode under InstantBattle. Holds the instant-battle rule catalogue (keyed by RuleID) plus title-wide defaults. Each rule defines wager economy (prize-pool burn) and battle settings: a combat-role → StatID mapping (which Character stat drives HP/Damage/Armor/AttackSpeed/CritChance/CritDamage/Dodge/AllMight), combat params (max rounds, block effect, crit/dodge clamps) and optional per-stat custom formulas. Stat/formula fields reference Character.Stats StatIDs; equipment bonuses (Item) key off the same StatIDs.

x-enum-descriptions: Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

CombatStatMapping.description: Maps the engine's combat roles to concrete character StatIDs (StatDefinition.StatID in CharacterDefinition.Stats). Lets a title decide which upgradable stat drives HP, damage, armor, etc. The same StatIDs key equipment flat/percent bonuses, so a remap automatically covers gear too. Any null/empty field inherits the built-in DefaultData default.

AllMightStatID.description: StatID of the global percent multiplier for HP/Damage (AllMight). Default: "AllMight".

ArmorStatID.description: StatID driving armor. Whether it reduces damage as a flat subtraction or as a fraction is decided by MatchCombatSettings.ArmorMode, which also decides the meaningful scale of the stat's values. Default: "Armor".

HealthStatID.description: StatID driving the fighter's max HP. Default: "Health".

x-enum-descriptions: Step: hold the previous point's value until the next one. Behaviour of an unset field.
Linear between adjacent points.
Geometric between adjacent points: lo * (hi/lo)^t.

CurvePoint.description: One breakpoint of a table curve.

AtStep.description: Step (level / rank / stage) at which this point takes effect. Empty = the point is ignored.

Value.description: Value at this point. Empty = the point is ignored.

x-enum-descriptions: Value does not change with the step. Same behaviour as an unset curve.
Additive in the value's own units: base + PerStep * (step - firstStep).
Additive share of the base: base * (1 + PerStepRate * (step - firstStep)). 0.1 = +10% of base per step.
Compounding: base * (1 + GrowthRate)^(step - firstStep).
Table of multipliers over the base: base * interpolate(Points, step).
Table of absolute values: interpolate(Points, step). The base is ignored.

EntryResourceRule.description: One entry-whitelist rule: a concrete resource (or resource family) with amount bounds. An entry position matches by Kind and identifiers; 0 in Min/Max = unbounded on that side.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog ID (for Kind = Item). Key in cfg.Item.Catalogs.

CurrencyID.description: Currency ID: a virtual currency (for Kind = VirtualCurrency, key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies) or a crypto currency (for Kind = CryptoCurrency, key in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies).

EntityID.description: Event ID within the system (for Kind = EventToken). null/empty = any event of that system.

ItemID.description: Item ID within the catalog (for Kind = Item). Key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[CatalogID].Items.

Kind.description: Resource kind this rule applies to.

MaxAmount.description: Maximum amount of the entry position. 0 = no upper bound.

MinAmount.description: Minimum amount of the entry position. 0 = no lower bound.

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

FormulaFactor.description: One multiplicative factor of a term. An empty factor equals 1 — for a product that IS the neutral element, so the publisher never types 1.

Argument.description: Argument of the variable (StatID, CurrencyID, ...). Its meaning is defined by the module.

Constant.description: The number when Kind=Constant. Empty = 1 (does not change the product).

Curve.description: The curve when Kind=Curve, evaluated at the context's step.

OnePlus.description: Wrap the value as (1 + value) — for '+50%'-style multipliers. Empty = use the raw value.

VariableID.description: Variable name when Kind=Variable. The vocabulary is owned by the consuming module and listed in that field's description; the platform does not validate it.

x-enum-descriptions: A number from the Constant field. Behaviour of an unset kind.
A named module variable (VariableID plus an optional Argument).
The value of the Curve field at the context's current step.

FormulaSpec.description: Expression: a sum of terms, each term = coefficient x product(factors). A factor references variables and curves, never another expression, so the graph is acyclic by construction. An unset expression evaluates to null, NOT to zero — the caller substitutes its own default.

Terms.description: Terms. Empty = the expression is not configured.

Factors.description: Factors, multiplied together. Empty = the term equals the coefficient.

InstantBattleDefinitions.description: Configuration of the instant-battle mode (immediate PvP simulation in PvPBattleEngine). Holds the rule catalog (Rules, keyed by RuleID) and title-wide defaults (Defaults) applied when a rule omits its own.

CreationDefaults.description: Title-wide offer-creation settings: creation cost, limits and anti-abuse controls. Applied block-level when a rule omits its own Creation. Unset here too = engine default (free, no limits). See MatchCreationSettings.

Defaults.description: Title-wide instant-battle defaults: role → StatID mapping, combat params and formulas. Applied per-block/per-role when a rule's Settings omits the same block. Anything unset here inherits engine built-in defaults. See InstantBattleSettings.

EntryDefaults.description: Title-wide instant-battle entry policy: which resources a player may commit to participate and within what bounds. Applied block-level when a rule omits its own Entry. Unset here too = engine default (any virtual currency). See MatchEntrySettings.

Rules.description: Instant-battle rule catalog. Key is RuleID (e.g. "InstantBattle1v1"). The client passes RuleID into CreateMatch/InstantBattle; a rule is allowed iff it has an entry here (or is the built-in InstantBattle1v1 when no config exists).

InstantBattleRule.description: One instant-battle rule. Stored in InstantBattleDefinitions.Rules by RuleID. Split into match-level economy (Economy, about the entry and reward) and battle settings (Settings). Any unset block inherits title/engine defaults.

Creation.description: Offer-creation settings for the rule: creation cost, limits and anti-abuse controls. Match-level (not battle). null = inherit InstantBattleDefinitions.CreationDefaults, then engine default (free, no limits). See MatchCreationSettings.

Description.description: Text description of the rule, for UI.

DisplayName.description: Display name shown in UI (localized or base).

Economy.description: Economy settings for the rule (reward burn share). Match-level: about the entry and reward. null = defaults (see MatchEconomySettings).

Entry.description: Entry policy for the rule: which resources a player may commit to participate and within what bounds. Match-level (not battle). null = inherit InstantBattleDefinitions.EntryDefaults, then engine default (any virtual currency). See MatchEntrySettings.

RuleID.description: Unique rule identifier (mirrors the Rules dictionary key). Passed by the client in CreateMatch/InstantBattle requests.

Settings.description: Battle settings for the rule: role → StatID mapping, combat params (rounds/block/clamps) and stat formulas. Each nested block is optional and inherits from InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults, then engine built-in defaults. See InstantBattleSettings.

InstantBattleSettings.description: Instant-battle settings block. Used both as InstantBattleRule.Settings (per-rule) and InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults (title-wide). All three blocks are optional and inherit: rule → InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults → engine built-in defaults.

Combat.description: Combat params (round count, block effect, chance clamps, etc.). null = inherit InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults block, then engine defaults (see MatchCombatSettings).

Formula.description: Custom combat-role formulas. Per-role: a role with a formula uses it; a role without falls back to InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults, then the engine's built-in default formula. See MatchStatFormula.

StatMapping.description: Combat-role → StatID mapping. Overlay per-role: set roles override the title default, unset roles inherit built-in defaults. See CombatStatMapping.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

MatchCombatSettings.description: Combat parameters of a PvP rule. All values have sensible defaults identical to the engine's historical behavior.

ArmorMode.description: How armor reduces damage. Default: Flat (the engine's historical behavior), so a title that does not set this field is unaffected.

BlockDamageMultiplier.description: Fraction of potential damage that still lands on a block (attack zone == defense zone). Default: 0.01 (1%).

DefaultCritMultiplier.description: Default crit-damage multiplier used when the crit-damage stat is absent/zero. Default: 1.5.

MaxArmorReduction.description: Upper bound on armor in PercentReduction mode (the lower bound is 0). Default: 0.9, i.e. at most 90% reduction. Not applied at all in Flat mode, where armor lives in damage units and 12 or 500 are both meaningful.

MaxCritChance.description: Upper clamp on the final crit chance (after stats and gear). Default: 0.6. Set to 1.0 to effectively disable.

MaxDodgeChance.description: Upper clamp on the final dodge chance (after stats and gear). Default: 0.4. Set to 1.0 to effectively disable.

MaxRounds.description: Max number of battle rounds. On timeout the fighter with more HP wins (tie = draw). Default: 50.

MinHitDamage.description: Minimum damage of a hit after armor reduction, in both ArmorModes. Last line of defence: armor above 100% (or above the raw damage) can never push damage negative, i.e. heal the defender. Default: 1. Size it against the title's damage scale - if early-level damage is comparable to the floor, the floor eats the whole reduction and armor stops reading until damage outgrows it.

MatchCreationSettings.description: PvP offer-creation settings: creation cost and anti-abuse controls. The creation cost is charged to the creator at CreateMatch SEPARATELY from the entry; it never enters the reward, is always sunk on a played match, and is refunded on cancel only when RefundCostOnCancel = true.

AllowPrivateMatches.description: Whether private offers (with TargetUserID) are allowed. Default: true.

Limits.description: Offer-creation limits. Only the CooldownSeconds (between creations) and DailyCap (per UTC calendar day) axes are enforced; other axes are ignored. null = no limits.

MaxMatchesPerOpponentPerDay.description: Max completed matches between the same pair of players per UTC calendar day (both directions). Anti-win-trading: limits resource funneling between alts. Authoritative check runs at InstantBattle. 0 = no limit.

MaxOpenMatches.description: Max simultaneously open offers per player (checked at CreateMatch). 0 = no limit.

OfferLifetimeSeconds.description: Offer lifetime in seconds since creation. An expired offer is hidden from listings, cannot be joined and does not count toward MaxOpenMatches; a timer refunds the creator's entry (status Expired), the creation cost per RefundCostOnCancel. Snapshotted into the match at creation (PvPMatch.ExpiresAt): editing the config does not affect already-open offers. 0 = never expires.

PriceOptions.description: Ways to pay for creating an offer. Dictionary key = PriceOption.OptionID. null/empty = free. Only the option's Cost.Standard is honored (premium fields ignored — the amount refundable on cancel must be deterministic and is snapshotted into the match doc). A store-paid option is not allowed: the fee may have to be refunded, and a store refund is not ours to issue.

RefundCostOnCancel.description: Whether to refund the creation cost when the creator cancels the offer (CancelMatch). Default: false — the cost is sunk (deters create/cancel spam). On a played match the cost is always sunk regardless of this flag.

MatchEconomySettings.description: Economy parameters of a PvP rule.

BurnRate.description: Fraction of the reward burned when granting it to the winner. burn = floor(reward * BurnRate); the winner gets the remainder. Default: 0.05 (5%). 0 = no burn.

MatchEntrySettings.description: Instant-battle entry policy: which resources a player may commit to participate and within what bounds. The entry is a ResourceBundle (currencies, stackable items, event tokens); both sides commit the same set and the winner receives double of each position (burn applies to virtual currencies only). Two control levels: type flags (AllowVirtualCurrency/AllowItems/AllowEventTokens = 'any resource of this type', no amount bounds) and the Allowed whitelist — when NON-empty it is authoritative: every entry position must match one of its rules (incl. Min/Max) and the type flags are ignored. Unstackable items are always rejected (refund/payout would recreate the instance and lose upgrade state). Event tokens: refunds/rewards credited to an ended event may become unclaimable after grace — whitelist long-lived systems (e.g. Season) only.

AllowCryptoCurrency.description: Allow the title's crypto currencies as an entry position (whole tokens, no USD amount). Default: false — a crypto match is money between players and must be enabled explicitly. The winner receives double the entry minus the developer's trade fee (CryptoCurrencyDefinition.PlayerTradeFeePercent); BurnRate does not apply to crypto. Ignored when Allowed is non-empty.

AllowEventTokens.description: Allow event tokens as an entry position. Default: false. Ignored when Allowed is non-empty.

AllowItems.description: Allow any stackable catalog items as an entry position. Unstackable items are always rejected. Default: false. Ignored when Allowed is non-empty.

AllowVirtualCurrency.description: Allow any of the title's virtual currencies as an entry position (no amount bounds). Default: true. Ignored when Allowed is non-empty.

Allowed.description: Whitelist of allowed entry resources with Min/Max bounds. When NON-empty it is authoritative: every entry position must match one of the rules and the type flags are ignored. Empty/null = type flags decide (amounts just > 0).

MaxPositions.description: Max number of positions in the entry bundle (Entries + EventTokens). Sanity cap against match-doc / dual-op bloat. Default: 10. 0 = no limit.

MatchStatFormula.description: Set of custom formulas for the engine's combat roles. Each role is optional: null = use the default formula (legacy or InstantBattleDefinitions.Defaults). Replace semantics (not merge). Role value = sum of terms; term = Coefficient * product(Factors). VOCABULARY for FormulaFactor.VariableID in this module: Stat (Argument = StatID, empty = this role's own mapped stat), RankMultiplier, AllMight, GearFlat (Argument = StatID), GearPercent (Argument = StatID). An unknown VariableID means NOT COMPUTED, not 0 — a typo shows up as 'my formula did not apply', never as a fighter with 1 HP. Factors reference Layer-1 stat values and multipliers, NOT other roles' final values (no cycles). Settings clamps/floors apply after the formula.

AttackSpeed.description: Formula for attack speed (initiative). null = default.

CritChance.description: Formula for crit chance (before MaxCritChance clamp). null = default.

CritDamage.description: Formula for crit-damage multiplier. null = default.

Dodge.description: Formula for dodge chance (before MaxDodgeChance clamp). null = default.

Health.description: Formula for max HP. null = default.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

PremiumTierDiscount.description: Percentage discount on ResourceConsume.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 - Discount) with Math.Ceiling rounding in player's favor. Applies only to Standard; ignored if PremiumTiers matches. Best matching tier wins, discounts do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierBonus.

Discount.description: Discount as a SHARE: 0.1 = -10%, 1.0 = free. Empty or 0 = no discount. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

PriceOption.description: A single way to pay for an entity. Platform-wide standard: everything with a configured price describes it as a PriceOptions dictionary whose key is the OptionID. Options exist because ResourceConsume.Standard is charged as a whole (AND), while a price across platforms is a choice (OR): a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. Platform duties split as "the client renders, the server allows": title config ships as one immutable artifact per (version, field set), so it cannot be filtered per request — the client hides options by AllowedPlatforms, while PriceOptionSelector.Select refuses a charge whose option is not available on the caller's platform.

AllowedPlatforms.description: Platforms this option is available on. Empty/null = all of them. Do not list Unknown: a client that did not report its platform only gets options with no platform restriction, i.e. those safe everywhere.

AssetPaths.description: Option assets (currency icon, discount badge). Key = asset slug.

Cost.description: What is charged for this option. Standard is the base; PremiumDiscounts / PremiumTiers behave as everywhere else. An entry of type Purchase means the option is paid in a store rather than with a player resource: the payment is verified before ResourceService and never enters the resource operation. No initializer on purpose — "unset" must differ from "set to empty"; an unset Cost means the option is free.

Name.description: Display name of the option ("For gold", "$0.99"). A localization key or a literal — resolved client-side by the rule own table → fallback table → the key itself.

OptionID.description: Payment-option identifier. If empty, the dictionary key is substituted (PriceOptionResolver) — the client selects an option by this ID, so an option without one would be unselectable.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceConsume.description: Consume direction container for ResourceOperation. Two mutually exclusive premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumTiers (priority) replaces Standard with the best matching tier's Resources via Replace, and PremiumDiscounts (fallback) applies a percentage discount to Standard only when no PremiumTier matched. Best matching tier wins, no stacking.

PremiumDiscounts.description: Percentage discount on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 - Discount)). Ignored if any PremiumTier matched — Replace takes over.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different price for premium players (different ItemID/CurrencyID/Target). Always Replace, single best matching tier wins. If matched, Standard is fully replaced and PremiumDiscounts is ignored; otherwise fallback to Standard + PremiumDiscounts.

Standard.description: Base — what to charge all players including F2P.

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Coin, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account. Requires only Amount — the price in whole Coin. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCoinPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted only by the store (Store.Purchase) for now; allowed only in Consume.

ScalarCurveSpec.description: Scalar curve f(base, step): how a value grows with a level, rank, stage or count. THE MODULE'S RULE: an empty field does nothing — an unset curve is the identity f(base,n)=base, an unset bound means there is no bound. All rates are shares (0.1 = +10%), never multipliers, so 0 and empty always mean the same thing.

Base.description: Base the curve is computed from. Empty = use the base supplied by the caller. Fill it only where the base is a publisher setting (a multiplier starting at 1.5, a table's value before its first point) — where the base comes from data (a stat value, a level price, an item bonus) leaving it empty is required, otherwise it overrides the real base.

GrowthRate.description: Compounding rate per step (Shape=Geometric): 0.1 = x1.1 per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

Interpolation.description: How to interpolate between points. Empty = Step.

MaxResult.description: Upper bound of the result. Empty = there is NO upper bound (not 0).

MinResult.description: Lower bound of the result. Empty = there is NO lower bound (not 0).

PerStep.description: Units added per step (Shape=PerStep). Empty or 0 = no growth.

PerStepRate.description: Share of the base added per step (Shape=PerStepRate): 0.1 = +10% of base per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

Points.description: Table breakpoints (Shape=Table or TableAbsolute). Empty = no growth.

Shape.description: Curve shape. Empty = Flat, i.e. no growth.

TailGrowthRate.description: Growth beyond the last table point (share per step). Empty = hold the last point's value.

value.description: Configuration of the title's PvP (Match) system. Grouped by battle mode: InstantBattle is the instant-battle container (rule catalog + title-wide defaults). Future match modes (tournament, async turn-based) are added here as sibling containers. Fully optional — absent config falls back to engine defaults (InstantBattle1v1 rule + DefaultData stat mapping), preserving legacy behavior.

InstantBattle.description: Instant-battle mode container: the rule catalog and title-wide defaults for immediate PvP. Future match modes (tournament, async turn-based) are added to MatchDefinitions as sibling containers. See InstantBattleDefinitions.
